 Search The Site More Than Half of New Yorkers Want Minimum Wage to Hit $30 an Hour More Than Half of New Yorkers Want Minimum Wage to Hit $30 an Hour
 CJ McIntyre CJ McIntyre Published: November 9, 2026 Canva Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 What do you think about making $30 an hour the new minimum wage? It might sound pretty good if you're collecting a paycheck, but it could also mean some big changes for businesses and consumers.
 Minimum Wage to Increase?
 According to a report from News 8 , a new study from Cornell University's School of Industrial and Labor Relations found that 60% of New Yorkers support raising the minimum wage to at least $30 an hour. That's right, more than half of the people surveyed think workers should be making at least $30 an hour.
 And if you think that's a big number, support is even higher in New York City, where 75% of those surveyed said they support the increase.
 Canva Minimum Wage Increase in New York New Yorkers Want a $30 Minimum Wage
 So why are so many people getting behind the idea? Well, just about everything seems to cost more these days. From groceries and gas to rent, utilities, and just about everything else, making ends meet isn't getting any easier.
 According to the report, the current minimum wage simply isn't keeping up with the cost of living. In most of New York State, the minimum wage is currently $16 an hour, while workers in New York City, Long Island, and Westchester County make $17 an hour.
 The survey also found that support for a $30 minimum wage is especially high among younger adults, with 83% of people between the ages of 25 and 34 supporting the increase. Support was also high among Black and Hispanic New Yorkers, as well as hourly workers.
 Interestingly, the report found that 79% of households earning less than $30,000 a year support the idea.
 Not Everyone Thinks $30 an Hour Is a Good Idea
 Of course, not everyone is on board with nearly doubling the minimum wage.
 Critics argue that requiring businesses to pay $30 an hour could put a serious financial strain on small businesses, potentially forcing some to cut jobs, reduce hours, raise prices, or even close their doors.
 SEE ALSO: The Largest Walmart in America is Located Right Here in New York 
 And that's something consumers could eventually feel, too. If businesses have to pay significantly more in wages, those added costs could find their way into the prices we pay.
 Meanwhile, New York's minimum wage isn't even scheduled to increase this January. An automatic increase planned for 2027 was put on hold after the state reported a loss of more than 31,000 jobs during the first half of the year.
 Governor Kathy Hochul is now proposing changes that would allow the minimum wage to increase again, including a proposed bump to $16.55 upstate and $17.60 downstate beginning March 1, 2027.
 Getty Images New York Governor Kathy Hochul What Do You Think?
 Is raising the minimum wage to $30 an hour a good idea? Could you imagine making $30 an hour at a job that currently pays minimum wage? It certainly sounds nice when you look at your paycheck, but what would it mean for the cost of running a business and the prices we pay every day?
 Would you support a $30 minimum wage, or do you think it would create more problems than it solves?
